formalDefinition:
An instance of the Pump Scheduling Cost Minimization is defined as a 3-tuple (T,D,P) where:
	the tank T=(c,v) is an ordered pair where c is an 
	integer representing the capacity of the tank, 
	and v is the current volume within the tank; 
	the demand configuration D=((d_0,...,d_{23}),
	(h_1,...,h_k),(r_on},r_off)) is an ordered triple 
	where (d_0,...,d_{23}) is a list of 24 integers 
	representing the water demand in gallons per hour
	for each hour of the day, (h_1,...,h_k) is a list 
	of integers representing the peak hours (using 
	0-based indexing), and (r_on,r_off) is an ordered
	pair of real numbers representing the 
	on-peak and off-peak energy costs per kWh; 
	and the pumps
	P=((n_1,f_1,p_1,s_1),...,(n_m,f_m,p_m,s_m)) is a
	list of m ordered 4-tuples where each 4-tuple 
	(n_i,f_i,p_i,s_i) represents a pump with name 
	n_i, flow rate f_i in gallons per hour, power 
	consumption p_i in kW, and startup cost s_i 
	in dollars.
Note: any water (e.g., gallons, liters, etc.) and cost units (e.g., $, euros, etc.) are assumed to be consistent throughout the instance definition
problemDefinition: Determine which pumps to activate each hour over a 24-hour period so that water demand is met, the storage tank never overflows or fails to supply the water demand, and the total energy cost (based on peak/off-peak tariffs plus pump startup costs) is minimized.
inputDescription: Tank state, hourly water demand, peak-hour tariffs, and pump specifications
outputDescription: The hourly pump activation schedule and its total cost, minimizing energy and startup costs

defaultSolver.solverName: Pump Scheduling Cost Minimization Dynamic Programming
defaultSolver.solverDefinition:
Models the 24-hour pump scheduling problem as a DAG where each node represents (hour, tank-level-bucket, previous-pump-mask). A forward pass computes the minimum-cost path from the initial state to any valid end state. The optimal schedule is recovered by backtracking through parent pointers.
The output certificate is a 2-section tuple: (total-cost, schedule) where total-cost is the total cost of the pump schedule, and schedule is a list of pump schedules (one per pump) where each pump schedule is a list of 24 binary values indicating whether that pump is on or off for each hour.

timeComplexity.Description: , H = 24 hours, B = tank buckets, n = number of pumps

defaultVerifier.verifierName: Default Pump Scheduling Cost Minimization Verifier
defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: Parses the pump schedule from the certificate, simulates the 24-hour tank trajectory using exact arithmetic, and accepts if: (1) the tank stays within [0, capacity] at every hour, (2) the reported cost matches the computed energy and startup costs within $0.01 tolerance.

defaultVisualization.visualizationName: Pump Scheduling Cost Minimization — DAG Animation
defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Animates the 24-hour optimal pump schedule, showing per-hour pump states, tank levels, and cumulative costs produced by the DAG dynamic programming solver.
